name: wingbox
description: Local code graph and blast radius analysis: module boundaries, dependents, impact of a change and the few files to read first, for Python, TypeScript, Rust, C#, Java, Go and Ruby repositories. Runs on your machine; no code leaves it.

interface.longDescription: Wingbox builds a code graph of the repository you work in and answers from it before the agent reads source files: which modules exist and where their boundaries are, what depends on a file, what a change could break two hops away, which three or four files to read first, and which dependencies cross an architecture layer. It parses Python, TypeScript and TSX, Rust, C#, Java, Go, Ruby and Ruby on Rails with tree-sitter, and writes an offline HTML map of the repository. Everything runs on your computer with the open-source wingbox command (MIT, on PyPI): no code, graph or question is sent anywhere. The plugin needs a local shell and the command, installed once with pipx install wingbox.
defaultPrompt: Build the code graph of this repository and tell me where to start reading.
What depends on this file, and what could break if I change it?
Which modules handle authentication, and which files should I read first?
